bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ's JSON API registration endpoints (POST /api/register and POST /api/v3.1/register, handled by Controller/Api/RegistrationController::create) create user accounts without ever checking the `security.enableRegistration` configuration flag that the HTML registration page enforces. An attacker can submit a crafted request directly to the API endpoint and register a new user account even when registration is disabled in the admin configuration (CWE-862 Missing Authorization on the registration action).
flaw_origin: Commit 94fc12e5852079a19dc98aab786cb7a5b1cc13ac ("feat(api): refactored REST API to register users", 2024-02-27, author+committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de>) created Controller/Api/RegistrationController.php (141 lines) with the `create()` action. The method from birth validates CSRF token (`hasValidToken`), email-domain allowlist, and required fields — but contains no check of `security.enableRegistration`; the route `v{apiVersion}/register` is wired in the same commit. The advisory's named sink (an API registration endpoint that skips the enableRegistration check enforced elsewhere) is born here; parent 80cc0a0aa2 lacks the controller.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author and committer Thorsten Rinne with a plain human message; no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot/AI identity anywhere on the object (grep NONE-94FC sentinel).
